newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BT wants to keep MCI's News Corp stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BT wants to keep MCI's News Corp stake.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) and its merger partner MCI Communications Corp wanted to keep their stake in Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, BT deputy chief executive Alan Rudge said in a television interview broadcast on Sunday.
"At the moment we'd like to keep that interest in the Murdoch activity," Rudge told the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme.
MCI, which is expected to complete its merger with BT later this year, owns just under nine percent of News Corp and has an option to increase that stake to 13.5 percent.

But MCI chief executive Bert Roberts told Reuters when the BT merger was announced in November 1996 that MCI would not increase its stake in News and would sell some of the interest in a satellite joint venture with News.
This led to market speculation that the alliance between MCI and News announced in May 1995 was going sour and would eventually lead to the sale of MCI's stake in News.
BT's Rudge said the merged group wanted to keep its links with News because they provided a bridge to the mult-media communications sector.
"It's an element of the bridge between today's telephony and and tomorrow's multi-media communiciations company," Rudge said.
"The close relationship we see is a very good thing without wanting to or anticipating that we will be going buying Hollywood studios or getting into the multi-media content business," he said.
"We won't sell it unless there are some contraints put on us which make it necessary," he said.
BT's merger with MCI must gain regulatory approval from British, European and U.S. regulators.
BT is barrred in Britain from using its network for entertainment purposes.
BT has denied that its MCI merger was a way of getting into the British satellite television business through the back door, saying that its holding in News was passive.
News Corp owns 40 percent of British Sky Broadcasting (BSkyB).
